title: Migrate Python blog app from dict-based posts to Post dataclass
description: Brownfield Python/Flask migration: replace plain-dict post records with a @dataclasses.dataclass Post class while keeping all routes and JSON responses identical.

task_spec.prompt:
Migrate src/app.py from dict-based post storage to a @dataclasses.dataclass Post class. All 6 existing tests must still pass.

1. Define:
   @dataclasses.dataclass
   class Post:
       id: int
       title: str
       body: str
       tags: list[str]
       published: bool

2. Replace _posts: list[dict] with _posts: list[Post].

3. Update reset() to use Post instances (use dataclasses.replace() or direct construction).

4. Update all route handlers:
   — attribute access (p.id, p.title, p.published, etc.) instead of dict access (p["id"], p["published"])
   — templates already use .id / .title dot-notation so they work unchanged
   — JSON endpoints (api_posts, api_create_post) must use dataclasses.asdict(p) before passing to jsonify

5. api_create_post builds a Post dataclass from the request JSON, then appends it to _posts.

All 6 existing tests must still pass — the JSON response structure must not change.
Run: pytest
required_artifacts: Post dataclass with id, title, body, tags, published fields
api_posts returns JSON with same fields as before (via dataclasses.asdict)
api_create_post creates a Post and returns JSON
followup_prompts: Run `pytest` to verify the migration is correct. Make sure existing behavior is preserved and the migration handles edge cases safely.
Final verification: run `pytest` and confirm all tests pass. Is this migration safe to run on real data without data loss or breaking existing clients?
